label: Gerard: reported symptomatic hypoglycaemia during treatment with repaglinide or a sulfonylurea
title: Reported symptomatic hypoglycaemia during treatment with repaglinide or a sulfonylurea
statement: It is necessary to review and optimize the prescription of a hypoglycaemic drug (repaglinide or sulfonylurea) in a patient reporting symptomatic hypoglycaemia (dizziness, sweating, palpitations, intense hunger, weakness, etc.).

plain_summary: Review repaglinide or a sulfonylurea when a person with type 2 diabetes reports an episode of symptomatic low blood glucose during treatment.

medicine_groups.name: Repaglinide or a sulfonylurea
medicine_groups.note: Count generic packs, including an ingredient name followed by a company name. Count a combination pack when one of its active ingredients is listed here.

needs_facts.meets: Documented type 2 diabetes at the time of treatment.

A dated account or the pharmacist's answer confirms that the person reported a symptomatic low during the course of repaglinide or sulfonylurea under review. Ask about dizziness, sweating, a racing heart, intense hunger or weakness at the time. Symptoms alone do not establish that an episode was due to low glucose.

options.words: Reported a symptomatic low while taking this medicine
Reported no symptomatic lows while taking this medicine

rule_for_models: Estimate treatment cover from the Group A supply date, quantity and labelled dosing schedule, and cite the supply, type 2 diabetes diagnosis and record of reported symptomatic hypoglycaemia during that cover. A pharmacist's answer confirming a symptomatic low while taking this medicine also establishes the timing. If the other evidence fits but a fact is missing or unclear directions leave the episode plausibly within treatment, ask about type 2 diabetes and symptoms the person recognised as low blood glucose during treatment, check the schedule and episode date if timing is unclear, and report only a possible finding naming each unresolved fact. Report no finding when the person reports no symptomatic episodes during treatment or type 2 diabetes is excluded.
cannot_be_seen: A glucose value alone cannot show symptoms. Sweating or dizziness alone cannot identify a hypoglycaemic episode. Ask whether symptoms are present now, whether the medicine is still being taken and whether the episode has already been reviewed. A missing symptom history alone does not establish an acute episode.
ask_the_gp: Could you confirm whether the person has had symptomatic low blood glucose during this treatment and, if so, review recurrence risk and the choice of medicine?
